history.summary: IDENTITY CAUTION: the Kundeshwari Temple at Kunda, near Deoghar, has almost no web footprint beyond visitor reviews and directory listings; its history, founding date and builder are UNVERIFIED. Devotee accounts describe it as an old shrine of Maa Kundeshwari (a form of the Divine Mother, also associated with Jagatdhatri/Kali) with adjacent temples of Shiva (a huge Shiva idol), Lakshmi Narayan, the Navagraha and Annapurna. One review claims Ram Krishna Paramhansa visited the temple - UNVERIFIED. Multiple reviews note poor maintenance and no renovation by the government or a trust, and describe it as a once-flourishing tourist spot now missing care. Treat all historical claims as provisional.

name: Kundeshwari Temple
town_description: Kunda is a locality a few kilometres from Deoghar town in Deoghar district, Jharkhand (Mohanpur block area). It is a rural neighbourhood best known locally for the Kundeshwari Mandir, the old shrine of the goddess Kundeshwari that devotees visit from Deoghar by auto. The temple sits in a calm, semi-rural setting away from Deoghar's main pilgrimage crowds.

travel.road: Reachable by auto from Deoghar auto stand; visitors report easy access by road (verify)
